text: A Wi-Fi client associated to an access point operates in which duplex mode?
choices: Full duplex, because modern Wi-Fi supports simultaneous send and receive
Half duplex, because a radio cannot listen on its own frequency while transmitting
Simplex, because the access point controls all transmissions
Full duplex on 5 GHz and half duplex on 2.4 GHz
explanation: A transmitting radio's own signal at its antenna overwhelms anything it is trying to hear, so it cannot receive while transmitting on the same frequency. Every Wi-Fi link is fundamentally half duplex regardless of its advertised rate, which is a large part of why real throughput is far below the number on the box.
